findings.title: Dereferencing possibly undefined first destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, the destructured value is undefined and this throws a TypeError whenever location is MeetLocationType, breaking event creation for users without any destination calendar.

findings.title: patch uses possibly undefined selectedCalendar
findings.body: In createEvent, `calendarId: selectedCalendar` in the follow-up patch call uses the raw find result (possibly undefined) instead of `selectedCalendar || "primary"` used for insert, so the patch can target an undefined calendar and fail to add the hangout link.

findings.title: Lookup compares externalCalendarId to itself
findings.body: In updateEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find compares against a falsy value and always returns undefined. The calendarId becomes undefined, and the update goes to an invalid calendar. The same bug is repeated in deleteEvent (line 317).

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are pushed into the organizer event
findings.body: teamDestinationCalendars is populated inside teamMemberPromises, which relies on the side effect of a map callback; and the list is pushed onto evt.destinationCalendar when COLLECTIVE. Duplicates or a null destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null when the organizer has none, so `?.push` silently does nothing) cause inconsistent behavior for collective events.

findings.title: Credential lookup duplicated and destination loop may create events for stale calendars
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents now loops over every destination calendar and creates an event per destination, including fetching credentials from DB, but the non-credentialId branch passes all matching credentials for the integration without filtering by externalId, so multiple destinations of the same integration can create duplicate events on the same calendar.

findings.title: createEvent in calendar services receives credentialId but Calendar interface change breaks existing implementations
findings.body: Calendar.createEvent signature changed to require a credentialId parameter, but many calendar services (e.g. office365, lark, caldav in lib/CalendarService.ts) still take only one argument. The interface contract is inconsistent with implementations and the parameter is silently ignored by most of them.

findings.title: Cancellation deletes calendar events but ignores promise results and errors
findings.body: apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) pushes unawaited promises; when the credential is missing from DB the reference is silently skipped, so cancelled bookings keep their calendar events without any signal.

findings.title: Required credentialId added to Calendar.createEvent breaks implementers and callers
findings.body: Making credentialId a required parameter on the Calendar interface forces every implementation and caller to change; the lib/CalendarService and other apps keep the old single-argument signature, which is a contract break that the type system only partially catches.
